sections.title: 21. Mod engineering · toolchain · purity
sections.summary: The mod-change trio (pack / lint / playtest), the content-addressed manifest, the multi-file purity and KV-prefix-ownership contracts, error location by real file, hot reload, and the single-source two-mods layering.

rules.text: After touching `data/` or `schemas/` you must run: `cargo run --example pack -- .ygg/mods/agent-seed`.

Lua static checks: `cargo run -p ygg-lint -- --pack .ygg/mods/agent-seed` (whole-pack mode, which also validates the `code.modules` declarations) or `cargo run -p ygg-lint -- .ygg/mods/agent-seed/mod.lua` (single-file mode); the result must be 0 errors / 0 warnings.

Smoke walk: `cargo run --example playtest -- .ygg/mods/agent-seed` (the all-1 walk must reach `[ENDING`). All-1 covers the happy path only — the acceptance standard for branches and map wording is `gates.mod-semantics-matrix` (`cargo test -p ygg-sandbox --test agent_seed_semantics`).
The manifest is content-addressed (sha256 + byteLength): editing `data/*.json` without recomputing the pack makes loading fail with a content-hash mismatch.

A multi-file Mod is registered only in the `code` section of `pack.json`: `entry` is not registered as a module, `modules` enumerates every file explicitly (no glob), and a missing `code` section means a single-file Mod (no migration needed for existing Mods). `require` works both at load time and at runtime (inside a handler) — `host.seal` only seals `ygg.on`, so a pure library may be loaded lazily; the price is that a module's top level may be a pure export surface only (see `mod.pure-export`). After changing any module file you must rerun pack (content-addressed: a byte-count or hash mismatch fails loading).
rules.basis: docs/design/mod-package.md (ex-DESIGN §3.2 "multi-file Mod"; the r5 documentation surface; the same-named subsection expands each item)

rules.text: A multi-file Mod's module chunk performs pure exports only (function and constant definitions) and does nothing with side effects: registration / state writes / output all live in the entry `mod.lua`. A module exposes registration as a function (`function M.install(deps)`) that the entry calls explicitly in order; touching `ygg.on` / `ygg.emit` / `ygg.narrate` / `ygg.choice` / `ygg.meta` / `ygg.kv.set` / `ygg.entity.spawn` / `ygg.entity.set_attribute` / `ygg.entity.add_tag` / `ygg.entity.remove_tag` / `ygg.fsm.define` / `ygg.narrative.node` / `ygg.narrative["goto"]` at a module's top level is refused (the static `YGG-MOD-EFFECT` rule and the runtime shadow table share the single list `ygg_modules::effects`); at the top level only pure reads are allowed (`ygg.data` / `ygg.ticks` / `ygg.kv.get` / `ygg.entity.has_tag` / `ygg.entity.get_attribute`); the entry chunk is exempt (it is the assembly manifest). Why: a handler's dispatch order equals the `ygg.on` registration order — letting a module register itself means "how the files are split / who is required first" decides runtime behavior, so splitting a file or reordering a `require` would change the dispatch order and refactoring would not preserve behavior. `require` is therefore usable at any time (including lazy-loading a pure library inside a handler), but lazy loading never relaxes the boundary: a lazily loaded module's top level is still pure exports. See `docs/design/mod-package.md` (ex-DESIGN §3.2 "Mod Package & Multi-File Purity Contract").
rules.basis: docs/design/mod-package.md (ex-DESIGN §3.2 "multi-file Mod"), side-effect boundary (semantics tightened in r1/r2/r3; the single source for both lists is ygg_modules::effects)

rules.text: In a multi-file Mod the KV prefixes are partitioned by ownership and each prefix has exactly one writer (a documentation convention; loading does not validate it): `fsm.*` is written only by the stdlib `ygg.fsm` and read-only for the Mod; `settings.*` is written only by `config.set`; `req.*` = the requirement table, `prop.*` = the proposal table, `lane.*` = the lane ledger, `ui.*` = presentation only (never in the summary, never affecting dispatch), and `task.*` / `verify.*` / `review.*` / `inbox.*` plus the bare key `ending` each have their own single writer. Two modules writing one prefix is implicit coupling — share through a module's return value instead.
rules.basis: docs/design/mod-package.md (ex-DESIGN §3.2 "KV prefix ownership"; user decision: documentation convention only, no load-time validation surface)

rules.text: Never "glue a multi-file Mod back into one file and then report errors": a module chunk name must carry the real file (`@src/core/util.lua`), a refusal the loader decides itself must carry the call site (`src/a.lua:3: <reason>`) and the require chain, and static checks must parse each module independently (a module's `local` never spans chunks, so gluing would invent a shared scope that does not exist at load time). A diagnostic whose line number does not match the real file is a defect.
rules.basis: docs/design/mod-package.md (ex-DESIGN §3.2 "error location: real file + real line number")

rules.text: Hot reload: single-shot mode loads from disk in every new process; an `open` (attach) receipt with `hotReload.source="resume"` proves the change is in effect.

The two mod paths are one Mod, not two copies: `.ygg/mods/agent-seed` is the single source of truth (the installed instance), and `packages/mods/agent-seed` is a git-tracked relative symlink to `../../.ygg/mods/agent-seed` — the stable packages-side entry, never an independent copy. `scripts/sync-seed-mod.sh` verifies the link target and the schema single-source (`packages/schema/schemas/`) and recomputes the content-addressed `manifest.json` (`--check` = read-only); the CI skeleton guard in `check.yml` still runs its diffs, but through the symlink they now compare the same files with themselves. The playbook is assembled, not duplicated: nine fragments under `data/playbook/` (a head plus eight chapter files) are joined by `mod.lua` in fixed order into 21 chapters — one fragment carries one to five chapters, section ids are globally unique across fragments, and this rule lives in the assembled `mod_engineering` chapter.

sections.title: 22. Host contract · literal ownership
sections.summary: The contract sections a Mod must declare (`agent` / `inboxRoutes` in pack.json, `settlement` / `drive` in config.json), the ownership boundary between contract and host literals, the choice payload type, and the fail-closed loading rule.

rules.text: The generic tooling (`src/playtest.rs`) hard-codes no event name / narrative prefix / summary key / entry payload / inbox field name / settlement switch / advancement threshold — it always reads the contract of the loaded Mod. The contract is mandatory: a missing section, a missing field, a wrong type or a non-positive integer fails loading (non-zero exit or `ok=false`); that is the deliberate fail-closed choice.
The `agent` section of `pack.json` has eight fields: entryEvent / choiceEvent / summaryEvent / endingPrefix / metaKey / rejectionPrefixes (at least one) / replayPrefix / defaultPayload.
The `inboxRoutes` section of `pack.json`: reserved keys externalIdField / payloadField / extMarker plus `<kind>` → `{action, fields[, write]}` (zero kinds is legal).
The `settlement` section (in `<config.json>`): requireEvents / requireNoFailedSteps / requireEnding / requireInboxConsumed.
The `drive` section (in `<config.json>`): maxSteps / stallLimit / stepsPerRequirement (positive integers).
`<config.json>` is the path declared by the `ygg:agent/config` entry in `pack.json` (`data/config.json` for the seed Mod).

Upgrading an old Mod means filling in the four sections (two in `pack.json`, two in `config.json`); `cargo run --example pack -- <mod dir>` validates their shape at pack time (only what is declared is validated).

Ownership boundary: event names / ending prefix / summary key / rejection and replay prefixes / inbox fields and routes / settlement switches / advancement thresholds belong to the contract and must be declared by the Mod; what the host may keep as literals is the run-directory file names, the coordination phase names running / closing / finalized, the decision-command timeout (`DECIDE_TIMEOUT`) and poll interval (`DECIDE_POLL_INTERVAL`), the three `--drive` modes, the five-file set (`pack.json` / `manifest.json` / `mod.lua` / `schemas/` / `data/`), and the kernel seams (`save` / `load` / `state`, and the reserved `ygg.choice_selected` route). Criterion: would this literal change with another Mod? If yes, it belongs to the contract.

Only applications bound to a specific Mod and the generator side may keep event-name / ending-prefix literals, and every such file declares "bound" or "generator-side" in its header: adventure.rs, clients/godot/rust/src/logic.rs, clients/godot/project/main.gd|session.gd, spike/godot/**, packages/client-web/src/{kernel,session,kernel-wasm}.ts and crates/ygg-wasm/smoke.mjs are bound to `packages/mods/test-adventure`; packages/pipeline/src/{prompt,types,pack}.ts and scripts-dev/mock-llm-stub.mjs are generator-side; the generic tooling of crates/ygg-sandbox|ygg-lint and the test fixtures under tests/ may not add literals, and `ygg.choice_selected` is the reserved event name checked by the kernel domain (the contract's `choiceEvent` must use it).

The payload of `ygg.choice_selected` must be a **JSON number** (`--payload '1'`); sending it as a string (`--payload '"1"'`) is rejected by the kernel domain as VALIDATION "option does not exist". Every other action's payload is a string. Menu selection is the **only** passing channel for the human-action gate — dispatching `proposal.accept` / `gate.approve` / `coordinate.submit` / `verify.submit` / `review.note` directly through `--event` is always refused (the receipt's first line is `[REJECTED:ACTION]`).
